queries: WITH per_scope AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count * 1.0 / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_per_scope FROM per_scope

responses.sql: WITH per_scope AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count * 1.0 / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_per_scope FROM per_scope

assumptions.assumption: Orders are counted once each (COUNT DISTINCT on orders.orderspivot), even if an order has several risk/margin records.
The average count per scope is taken over scopes that have at least one matched order. Scopes with no matches don't appear, because the inner joins drop them.
Users are matched to orders on userstamp, which is assumed unique. Orders or risk records with no matching row are dropped (inner joins). Share and ratio are shown as unrounded decimals.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin records (join rows) per scope, so an order with several risk records is counted several times.

assumptions.assumption: An order counts once per scope even if it has several risk/margin rows, so the query uses COUNT(DISTINCT orders.orderspivot).
The average count per scope is taken over the scopes that appear in the result (scopes with at least one matched order). Scopes with no matches are excluded.
Inner joins drop unmatched rows, as the request says to ignore anything that doesn't match.

alternatives.interpretation: Count matched risk/margin rows (order-risk pairs) per scope, so an order with several risk rows counts several times.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, order_count, order_count * 1.0 / SUM(order_count) OVER () AS share_of_total, order_count * 1.0 / AVG(order_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_per_scope FROM c

assumptions.assumption: Each order is counted once per scope, even if several risk/margin records point to it (COUNT DISTINCT on the order key).
Only scopes with at least one matched order appear. The average per scope is taken over those scopes, because inner joins drop unmatched rows.
Shares and ratios are unrounded decimals, with counts cast to avoid integer division.
